title: IE evidence for sub-shells (period 3 dips); Mass spectrometry of elements; The mole and Avogadro constant; Empirical and molecular formulae; Concentration and standard solutions; Molar gas volume and Avogadro's law; Ideal gas equation and gas laws; Titrations and solution calculations
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Eduqas A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: AS02#t2 term and clue written for the game; AS02#t1 term and clue written for the game; AS06#t2 term and clue written for the game; AS02#t3 term and clue written for the game. assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Mass-to-charge ratio
items.clue: The quantity written m/z, plotted on the x-axis of the spectrum.

items.label: Mass spectrometer
items.clue: Instrument that turns particles into positive ions and sorts them.

items.label: Sub-shell
items.clue: A division of a main level, such as 3s or 3p, with its own energy.

items.label: Relative abundance
items.clue: Shown by peak height: how much of each isotope an element contains.

questions.stem: How many atoms are there in 0.500 mol of water, H₂O? (N_A = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹)
A compound contains 40.0% carbon, 6.7% hydrogen and 53.3% oxygen by mass. Its Mr is 60.0. What is its empirical formula?
questions.explanation: In 100 g: 3.33 mol C, about 6.6–6.7 mol H, 3.33 mol O. ÷ smallest: 1 : 2 : 1.

questions.stem: What amount of sodium hydroxide is present in 25.0 cm³ of NaOH(aq) in which [NaOH] = 0.100 mol dm⁻³?
A gas syringe contains 2.20 cm³ of an ideal gas at 20 °C and 1.20 × 10⁵ Pa. What amount of gas does it contain? (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)

Two identical sealed flasks are at the same temperature and pressure. One is filled with methane, CH₄, and the other with chlorine, Cl₂. The methane flask contains 5.00 × 10²² atoms in total. How many atoms does the chlorine flask contain? (Ar: H 1.0, C 12.0, Cl 35.5)
questions.explanation: Equal molecules: 5.00 × 10²² ÷ 5 = 1.00 × 10²² CH₄ molecules, so 1.00 × 10²² Cl₂ molecules = 2.00 × 10²² atoms.

questions.stem: Vinegar (ethanoic acid, a weak acid) is in the conical flask. Sodium hydroxide is added from the burette. Which indicator should be used, and what is the colour change at the end point?

options.text: Methyl orange, from red to yellow
Either indicator, because the acid and alkali react in a 1 : 1 ratio

questions.explanation: Weak acid + strong base: phenolphthalein. It is colourless in the acid and turns pink when a slight excess of alkali is present.

questions.stem: The mass spectrum of element E shows three peaks from singly charged atomic ions: m/z 24 (relative abundance 100), m/z 25 (relative abundance 12.7) and m/z 26 (relative abundance 13.9). What is the relative atomic mass of E, calculated from these data?
After the dip, the rise resumes: silicon's first ionisation energy is 787 kJ mol⁻¹, higher than aluminium's 578 kJ mol⁻¹. Why?

options.text: Silicon's electron is removed from 3s, which is lower in energy than aluminium's 3p.
Silicon's two 3p electrons are paired in one orbital, which holds them more firmly.
Silicon atoms are larger, so there is more space for the nucleus to attract its electrons.
Both electrons come from 3p, but silicon has one more proton and similar shielding.

questions.explanation: Same sub-shell, similar shielding, greater nuclear charge: the attraction is stronger, so more energy is needed.

questions.stem: A student writes: 'Mr of carbon dioxide, CO₂ = 44.0 g mol⁻¹'. Which comment on this statement is correct?

options.text: It is correct: Mr and molar mass are one and the same quantity.
The unit is wrong: Mr is the mass of one molecule in grams.
The unit is wrong: Mr is measured in atomic mass units.
The unit is wrong: Mr is a ratio of masses, with no unit.

questions.explanation: Mr compares a CO₂ molecule with 1/12 of a carbon-12 atom; units cancel. M(CO₂) = 44.0 g mol⁻¹.

questions.stem: A compound of aluminium and sulfur contains 35.93% aluminium and 64.07% sulfur by mass. What is its empirical formula? Data: Ar Al 27.0, S 32.1.
questions.explanation: Divide each mass by its atomic mass: Al 1.33, S 2.00. Ratio 1 : 1.50; × 2 = 2 : 3.

questions.stem: A student prepares 100.0 cm³ of 0.200 mol dm⁻³ CuSO₄(aq) by placing 3.19 g of CuSO₄(s) in a 100.0 cm³ volumetric flask, dissolving it in some distilled water, adding distilled water to the mark and mixing. The concentration is later found to be less than 0.200 mol dm⁻³. Which of the following could explain this result?

options.text: The flask still held some distilled water from rinsing when the CuSO₄ was added.
Water was added until the bottom of the meniscus was above the mark.
Half of the solution was poured into a beaker before its concentration was measured.
The CuSO₄ dissolved completely, so no solid could be seen in the flask.

questions.explanation: Overfilling makes the volume more than 100.0 while the amount stays 0.0200 mol, so c = n/V falls.

questions.stem: A fixed mass of an ideal gas occupies 2.00 × 10⁻³ m³ at 1.00 × 10⁵ Pa and 27 °C. It is compressed to 5.00 × 10⁻⁴ m³ and at the same time its temperature rises to 87 °C. What is its new pressure?
questions.explanation: p₂ = 1.00 × 10⁵ × 4.00 × (360/300) = 4.80 × 10⁵ Pa. Compressing and heating both raise the pressure.
